title.es: Analizar la letra de una canción original

es: Analizar el tema, el tono (incluidos los matices agridulces) y dos recursos figurados (símil, metáfora, personificación) en la letra de una canción original, leída y escuchada, e inferir qué efecto produce cada recurso.

teaching.en: This lyric is about the bus ride home at night, and its bittersweet mood comes from the contrast between the warm lights and the long, empty streets.
teaching.es: Esta letra trata del viaje a casa en autobús por la noche, y su ambiente agridulce nace del contraste entre las luces cálidas y las calles largas y vacías.
teaching.explanationEs: Lyric es el texto de una canción; bittersweet mezcla alegría y tristeza, y se explica con un contraste.
segments: This lyric is about the bus ride home at night, and its bittersweet mood
comes from the contrast between the warm lights and the long, empty streets.
teaching.audioText: This lyric is about the bus ride home at night, and its bittersweet mood comes from the contrast between the warm lights and the long, empty streets.

teaching.en: The theme is comfort: the singer wants to feel safe at home, although an undertone of tiredness suggests how long the day has been.
teaching.es: El tema es el consuelo: la cantante quiere sentirse segura en casa, aunque un matiz de cansancio sugiere lo largo que ha sido el día.
teaching.explanationEs: El tema es la idea central; el undertone es lo que se siente debajo, sin que la letra lo diga.
segments: The theme is comfort: the singer wants to feel safe at home,
although an undertone of tiredness suggests how long the day has been.
teaching.audioText: The theme is comfort: the singer wants to feel safe at home, although an undertone of tiredness suggests how long the day has been.

teaching.en: Each verse adds a detail about the journey, and the chorus repeats “take me home”, which makes that wish the emotional centre of the song.
teaching.es: Cada estrofa añade un detalle del viaje y el estribillo repite «llévame a casa», lo que convierte ese deseo en el centro emocional de la canción.
teaching.explanationEs: La repetición del estribillo subraya la idea principal; las estrofas la desarrollan.
segments: Each verse adds a detail about the journey, and the chorus repeats “take
me home”, which makes that wish the emotional centre of the song.
teaching.audioText: Each verse adds a detail about the journey, and the chorus repeats “take me home”, which makes that wish the emotional centre of the song.

teaching.en: “The city is a sleeping giant” is a metaphor, because it says that one thing is another without using like or as.
teaching.es: «La ciudad es un gigante dormido» es una metáfora, porque dice que una cosa es otra sin usar like ni as.
teaching.explanationEs: Metáfora: A es B, sin like ni as; aquí la ciudad parece enorme y tranquila.
segments: “The city is a sleeping giant” is a metaphor, because it
says that one thing is another without using like or as.
teaching.audioText: “The city is a sleeping giant” is a metaphor, because it says that one thing is another without using like or as.

teaching.en: “Like a paper boat on a slow, warm river” is a simile, and its tender image makes the singer sound small but calm.
teaching.es: «Como un barquito de papel en un río lento y cálido» es un símil, y su imagen tierna hace que la cantante parezca pequeña pero tranquila.
teaching.explanationEs: Símil: compara dos cosas con like o as; cada recurso produce un efecto, no solo decora.
segments: “Like a paper boat on a slow, warm river” is a simile,
and its tender image makes the singer sound small but calm.
teaching.audioText: “Like a paper boat on a slow, warm river” is a simile, and its tender image makes the singer sound small but calm.

teaching.en: The streetlamps whisper advice to the traveller, so the lyric uses personification to make the night sound friendly rather than frightening.
teaching.es: Las farolas susurran consejos al viajero, así que la letra usa personificación para que la noche suene amistosa y no aterradora.
teaching.explanationEs: Personificación: un objeto hace algo que solo hacen las personas; aquí cambia la sensación de la noche.

prompt.es: Lee la letra y elige cuál es su tema.

choices.text: Coming home safely after a long day.
Feeling lost in a city that is too big.
Waiting for a friend who is very late.

feedback.es: El estribillo repite «take me home» y el resto describe la ciudad de noche con calma: el tema es volver a casa con tranquilidad.

hint.es: Fíjate en el estribillo: Take me home.

origin.text: The city is a sleeping giant tonight, / and I am a small light moving through its dreams. / The streetlamps whisper, “Go slow, go slow.” / Take me home, take me home, / like a paper boat on a slow, warm river.

prompt.es: Elige qué recurso es «The streetlamps whisper».

choices.text: Metaphor: the lamps are said to be people.
Personification: lamps do something only people do.
Simile: the lamps are compared to people with like.

feedback.es: Las farolas no pueden susurrar: darles una acción humana es personificación, no metáfora ni símil.

hint.es: Las farolas hacen algo que solo hacen las personas.

prompt.es: Completa: «El estribillo repite el deseo principal de la canción.»

feedback.es: El chorus es la parte que vuelve entre las estrofas y subraya la idea principal.

hint.es: Es la parte que vuelve entre una estrofa y otra.

origin.text: Each verse adds a new detail about the journey, while the ___ repeats the main wish of the song at the end of every section.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada verso con el recurso o el tono que transmite.

pairs: The moon is a silver plate.
The wind sings in the trees.
Her voice was like warm tea.
The house smells of rain and old books; nothing hurts tonight.

feedback.es: Sin like ni as, «is» da una metáfora; con like es un símil; si el viento canta hay personificación; y un ambiente sin conflicto crea un tono sereno.

pairs: The moon is a silver plate.
The wind sings in the trees.
Her voice was like warm tea.
The house smells of rain and old books; nothing hurts tonight.

prompt.es: Escucha esta letra y elige cuál es su tono.

choices.text: Bittersweet, with a strong feeling of loss.
Tense and worried, as if something might go wrong.
Tender and calm, with a feeling of safety.

feedback.es: La lluvia como canción, el olor a pan, la madre cantando y el reloj amistoso crean un ambiente tierno y tranquilo, sin ninguna pérdida.

origin.audio: The rain is a song on the roof. The kitchen smells of bread, and my mother is singing. Nothing is wrong tonight, nothing is late. The clock on the wall is an old friend who never hurries, and the window holds the dark like a warm blue blanket. Stay a little longer, stay a little longer, while the whole house hums.

prompt.es: Lee la letra y elige su tema.

choices.text: Saying goodbye to a hometown and its people.
Returning to a hometown after many years.
Missing a train that has already left.

feedback.es: El hablante se despide de su ciudad y promete llevarla consigo: el tema es decir adiós a un lugar querido.

origin.text: Tomorrow I leave this town, / but I will carry its streets in my pocket. / The baker waves, the river keeps its secret, / and the train is already humming in the dark. / Wait for me, old bridge, wait for me.

prompt.es: ¿Qué matiz sugieren los últimos versos frente al tono alegre del principio?

choices.text: A happy tone that grows stronger as the day goes on.
A bittersweet undertone: the cheerful mood hides some worry.
A plainly sad tone that replaces the happy morning.

feedback.es: Las monedas contadas dos veces y las últimas naranjas envueltas despacio dejan un matiz de preocupación bajo la alegría: el tono es agridulce.

origin.text: The morning is a bowl of golden light, / and the market wakes with a hundred voices. / Stay a little longer, stay a little longer, / the day is young and the people are kind. / But the baker counts his coins twice, / and the old seller wraps her last oranges slowly, / as if the day could wait for her.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué tres recursos aparecen.

choices.text: Two similes and a personification.
A metaphor, a repetition and a simile.
Personification, a simile and a metaphor.

feedback.es: The oranges laugh da una acción humana a las naranjas (personificación), as quick as birds compara con as (símil) y the evening is a blue coat es una metáfora.

origin.audio: The oranges laugh in their wooden boxes, and my grandmother's hands are as quick as birds. Later, the evening is a blue coat that the whole town puts on.

prompt.es: Completa: «Bajo la melodía alegre corre un matiz de tristeza.»

feedback.es: Un undertone es un matiz que se siente debajo de las palabras, sin que la letra lo diga de forma explícita.

origin.text: The singer never says that she is sad. Instead, a gentle ___ of sadness runs under the cheerful melody, so the listener feels it without being told.

prompt.es: Ordena: «El matiz agridulce viene del contraste en la última estrofa.»

answer.text: The bittersweet undertone comes from the contrast in the last verse

feedback.es: Comes from the contrast explica de dónde viene el matiz: el contraste entre un ambiente alegre y los últimos versos preocupados.

prompt.es: ¿Qué sugiere el final de la letra sobre la actitud de la hablante?

choices.text: She is sad but keeps hoping the person will return.
She is resigned: she accepts that the person will never return.
She is bitter: she blames the person for leaving her alone.

feedback.es: Mantener la luz encendida «like a small promise» muestra esperanza, y la noche larga revela la tristeza: no hay resignación ni rencor.

origin.text: The house is a heavy coat I cannot wear, / and your chair is still waiting by the door. / I keep the light on, like a small promise, / though I know the night will be long.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué efecto crean estas imágenes.

choices.text: A calm, quiet atmosphere, as if the house were resting.
A tense atmosphere, as if something is about to happen.
A playful atmosphere, as if the furniture were playing a game.

feedback.es: Un reloj que tose, una puerta que se cierra sola y una casa que contiene el aliento crean tensión e inquietud.

origin.audio: The clock coughs in the hall, and the stairs wait in the dark. Somewhere upstairs, a door that nobody touched is slowly closing, and the whole house is a held breath.

prompt.es: Completa: «La noche es un amigo paciente» es una metáfora.

feedback.es: Decir directamente que A es B, sin like ni as, es una metáfora; con like sería un símil.

origin.text: “The night is a patient friend” describes the night as a friend without using like or as, so it is a ___.
